<a id="identification-where-bounded--有界之处的辨识"></a>
# Identification where bounded

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`identification-where-bounded` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](identification-where-bounded.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> A bounded prefix fixes the course at an exact length. With the bound given, induction is deduction; not given, extrapolation by the least bound is right from 2N − 1 on, as early as any can be: the bound buys silence, not speed. Finite names name the split that makes sense, with no quotient.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Two periods (Fine–Wilf): a course with period p + 1 that comes back after Q steps at each of its first p steps comes back after Q steps at every step; two courses repeating from i, i′ with periods q + 1, q′ + 1 that agree before (i + q + 1) + (i′ + q′) agree at every step. (`Becoming.Identification.period_extends`, `Becoming.Identification.lassos_agree`, `Becoming.Learning.Lasso`)
2. A course has at most N states (StatesBelow o N: every moment is one state with some moment before N) exactly where it repeats from some step i with some period q + 1, i + q + 1 ≤ N. (`Becoming.StatesBelow`, `Becoming.SameAhead`, `Becoming.Identification.statesBelow_iff_lasso`)
3. Two courses with at most N and at most N′ states that agree before N + N′ − 1 agree at every step; prefixes are equal exactly where the courses agree before their length; so the prefix before N + N′ − 1 fixes the course. (`Becoming.Identification.bounded_agree`, `Becoming.Identification.prefix_eq_iff`, `Becoming.Identification.prefix_fixes`, `Becoming.Learning.prefixOf`)
4. Given two values: for every T, a course with one state and one with at most T + 1 share their prefix before T and differ at T; for every M, two courses with at most M + 2 states share their prefix before M + M + 2 and differ there. For every M and M′, a course with at most M + 1 states and one with at most M′ + 1 share their prefix before M + M′ and differ at step M + M′: the length N + N′ − 1 is exact for every pair of bounds. (`Becoming.Identification.prefix_short`, `Becoming.Identification.mark`, `Becoming.Identification.prefix_short_twice`, `Becoming.Identification.bounded_agree_exact`)
5. With at most N states, two moments are one state exactly where what follows them agrees for N + N − 1 steps: the states are read off a finite prefix. (`Becoming.Identification.sameAhead_iff_below`)
6. On a course with at most N states, a lasso (i, q) within N (i + q + 1 ≤ N) that accords on the prefix before N + N − 1 accords at every step; with values decided, a lasso candidate within N that misses nowhere before N + N − 1 misses nowhere at all, and one always does: induction is deduction. (`Becoming.Identification.lasso_of_fits`, `Becoming.Identification.bounded_induction`, `Becoming.Identification.bounded_hypothesis`, `Becoming.Learning.lasso`, `Becoming.Learning.Accords`, `Becoming.Learning.MissesAt`)
7. The extrapolation given N (withBound N) stays silent before N + N − 1 and then proposes by the first lasso candidate within N that the prefix bears out; on every course with at most N states it misses nowhere and is right at every step from N + N − 1 on. (`Becoming.Identification.withBound`, `Becoming.Identification.Fits`, `Becoming.Identification.BorneOut`, `Becoming.Identification.firstFit`, `Becoming.Identification.withBound_accords`, `Becoming.Identification.withBound_exact`)
8. None can always propose sooner: given two values, no extrapolation misses nowhere on every course with at most M + 2 states and proposes at step M + M + 2 on each. (`Becoming.Identification.withBound_earliest`)
9. withBound 2 is right about the two-valued negation at every step from 3 on; where other moves every value, the course answering the extrapolation given N has more than N states. (`Becoming.Identification.negation_derived`, `Becoming.Negation.course`, `Becoming.Identification.answer_exceeds_bound`)
10. With at most N states and values decided, a lasso candidate (a, b) within N, a ≤ s, missing at no step from s to before s + (N + N − 1) misses at no step from s on; extrapolation by elimination over the lasso candidates proposes and is right at every step from N + (N + N − 1) · tri N on; on a lasso course there is such a step. (`Becoming.Identification.no_miss_persists`, `Becoming.Identification.byElimination_rests`, `Becoming.Identification.rests_of_lasso`, `Becoming.Learning.byElimination`, `Becoming.Learning.lassos`, `Becoming.Learning.tri`)
11. Where an orbit is held by a list l, the same holds with N the length of l. (`Becoming.Identification.held_byElimination_rests`, `Becoming.Law.orbit`)
12. For a list l closed under the law, members s, s′ have the same future through the map exactly where those futures agree for l.length + l.length − 1 steps; where l holds every configuration, naming by the future through the map of that length (Law.name) makes sense with no quotient, carries the law and, values decided, decides likeness. (`Becoming.Law.SameFuture`, `Becoming.Law.sameFuture_iff_below`, `Becoming.Law.name`, `Becoming.IdentifiesAlike`, `Becoming.Law.name_identifiesAlike`, `Becoming.Law.name_carries`, `Becoming.Law.decideAlike`)
13. Moore's bound: under a determined law on a list of N members closed under it, with the members' values compared decidedly, two members have the same future through the map exactly where they agree for N − 1 steps. Agreeing for k + 1 steps (Law.AgreeTo) is a chain of equivalences, each finer than the one before; members with different values make two classes, each strict refinement adds one, and members pairwise apart are no more than the list, so the chain stops refining within N − 2 steps and, the law being determined, never refines again. With no decision, that they agree everywhere is refuted by nothing. Exact for every N ≥ 2: on a path of N positions to a last one that stays, the map taking only whether the last is reached, the first two positions agree for N − 2 steps and differ at the next. Two moments of a history with at most N states and decided values are one state exactly where they agree for N − 1 steps. (`Becoming.Law.AgreeTo`, `Becoming.Law.agreeTo_iff`, `Becoming.Law.agreeTo_refining`, `Becoming.Law.AgreeTo.decided`, `Becoming.Law.AgreeTo.steady_on`, `Becoming.Law.sameFuture_iff_classes`, `Becoming.Law.sameFuture_classes_unrefuted`, `Becoming.Law.sameFuture_classes_exact`, `Becoming.Identification.sameAhead_iff_classes`, `Becoming.DistinctUnder`, `Becoming.DistinctUnder.length_le`, `Becoming.Refining`, `Becoming.SteadyAt`, `Becoming.Refining.grow`, `Becoming.Refining.steady_within`, `Becoming.not_not_within`)
14. Moore's bound with no premise: under a determined law on a list of N members closed under it, two members have the same future through the map exactly where they agree for N − 1 steps, with no value compared decidedly. What is decided is the positions, not the values: the law is read on the positions of the list (Law.orbit_memberAt; finitely many existences chosen together, with no axiom of choice), whose equality is decided; joining, pair by pair, the two positions the prefix's agreement joins at each step (Law.merge, Law.joinOrbits) gives a labelling of the positions whose labels have one value each (Law.joinOrbits_sound); the labelling agrees for N − 1 steps, Moore's bound with decided values holds for it, and it carries over to the values. Two moments of a history with at most N states are one state exactly where they agree for N − 1 steps, with no premise too. (`Becoming.Law.orbit_memberAt`, `Becoming.Law.choose_below`, `Becoming.Law.merge`, `Becoming.Law.SoundFor`, `Becoming.Law.merge_sound`, `Becoming.Law.joinOrbits`, `Becoming.Law.joinOrbits_sound`, `Becoming.Law.joinOrbits_joins`, `Becoming.Law.sameFuture_iff_within`, `Becoming.Identification.sameAhead_iff_within`)
15. The rest step needs no bound: the extrapolation by the least bound (leastBound), given no bound, proposes by the first lasso candidate the prefix bears out within the least bound within which one is (leastFit); it is right at every step from N + N − 1 on of every history with at most N states, for every N (leastBound_exact): what it finds is within the true bound, since the true candidate is borne out, and a candidate within N borne out before N + N − 1 accords everywhere. Given two values, no extrapolation, given the bound or not, is right at step M + M + 2 on every history with at most M + 2 states (rest_earliest), so N + N − 1 is the optimal rest step for every extrapolation, and being given the bound does not move it. What the bound buys is silence: no extrapolation is both right at step 1 on every history with one state and missing at no step of every history with two states (rest_without_bound_missed); the extrapolation given the bound stays silent before N + N − 1 and misses nowhere (the seventh law). (`Becoming.Identification.orFit`, `Becoming.Identification.leastFit`, `Becoming.Identification.leastFit_sound`, `Becoming.Identification.leastFit_within`, `Becoming.Identification.leastBound`, `Becoming.Identification.leastBound_exact`, `Becoming.Identification.rest_earliest`, `Becoming.Identification.rest_without_bound_missed`)
16. Extrapolation by elimination rests at a cubic step: on the two-valued negation along a cycle of N = 2m + 3 places (oddCycle), with at most N states, it misses at step (N³ − N)/4 (byElimination_missed_late), each even shift before the period N taking a whole turn; so no step before (N³ − N)/4 bounds its rest on every two-valued history with at most N states (byElimination_rest_cubic). (`Becoming.Identification.oddCycle`, `Becoming.Identification.oddCycle_below`, `Becoming.Identification.turnHeld`, `Becoming.Identification.even_shift_runs`, `Becoming.Identification.odd_shift_runs`, `Becoming.Identification.unit_shift_missed`, `Becoming.Identification.turn_walk`, `Becoming.Identification.turn_diagonals`, `Becoming.Identification.byElimination_missed_late`, `Becoming.Identification.byElimination_rest_cubic`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom; no premise beyond the bound on states, written into each theorem (StatesBelow o N, or a world held by a list of length N).
- The extrapolation and deciding likeness by names need the values through the map decided (DecidableEq O, DecidableEq R), the ‘values decided’ of learning-by-refutation; so does the extrapolation by the least bound (leastBound); bounded_agree, lasso_of_fits, Law.name_identifiesAlike, rest_earliest and rest_without_bound_missed do not. The sixteenth law is stated on two values (Bool), which are decided.
- Only determined laws and single courses through a map are stated; branching frames and probabilities are not.
- Moore's bound in its counting form (Law.sameFuture_iff_classes, Identification.sameAhead_iff_classes) needs the members' values compared decidedly (Decided for each pair of the list, no decision procedure); Law.sameFuture_iff_within and Identification.sameAhead_iff_within do not: they decide positions (equality in Nat), not values. Law.sameFuture_classes_unrefuted does not, and states only that agreeing everywhere is refuted by nothing.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- The bound must hold (the course has at most N states); the extrapolation need not be given it (the fifteenth law), but with no bound no prefix fixes the next value.
- The exact rest step of extrapolation by elimination is not shown: for odd N it comes after (N³ − N)/4 (the sixteenth law) and is at most N + (2N − 1)·tri N (the tenth law), so it is cubic; exhaustive search over two-valued histories with at most N states (N ≤ 17) and three-valued ones (N ≤ 9) finds the worst rest step (N³ − N)/4 + 3 for odd N ≥ 3, a computation, not a proof. The optimum over extrapolations is 2N − 1 (the fifteenth law).
- **Counterexample:** prefix_short: a course with one state and one with T + 1 share their prefix before T and differ at T; prefix_short_twice: two courses with M + 2 states (marking every M + 2 and every M + 1 steps) share their prefix before M + M + 2 and differ there; bounded_agree_exact: for every M and M′, the course marking one step in every M + 1, with a mark at M + M′, and the course following it before M′ and unmarked from then on share their prefix before M + M′ and differ there; answer_exceeds_bound: the course answering the extrapolation given N exceeds N states; Law.sameFuture_classes_exact: for every M, on the path of M + 2 positions to a last one that stays, the map taking only whether the last is reached, the first two positions agree for M steps and differ at step M; byElimination_missed_late: on the two-valued negation along a cycle of N = 2m + 3 places extrapolation by elimination misses at step (N³ − N)/4. <a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Ren's speculation on 12 October 2026, ‘the full "truth" can be derived, situationally, including the cognition/controller part’, and the later ‘keep prove to the deepest … for the open questions, if they need to be answered to move forward, answer them’: this answers the last two questions Description, Diagonal and Context left open, deriving the law from a finite prefix and naming with no axiom the classes of the split that makes sense. Extrapolation by elimination gives the side with no bound (no prefix fixes the next value; the extrapolation's coming to rest is unrefuted); this gives the side with the bound given, its exact boundary, and the step by which the extrapolation not given the bound rests, which the bound gives and the extrapolation's prefix does not show. Known results: Fine and Wilf's two periods (1965), Moore's finite experiments (1956), Gold's identification in the limit (1967), here reproved in the core with no axiom and connected. Readings (the AI's, adopted on Ren's delegation, DELEGATED-CHOICES D34; the finite name taken by Ren on 16 October 2026 as an analogy, “take 2”: the theorem is that within a bound kinds have finite names, and 名可名 is an analogy only): a finite prefix is a projection, which the bound makes lose nothing of the course; the controller is inside the bounded world, and only a world answering it defeats it, which exceeds the bound; with a bound, a class's name is its finite future; being given the bound and not being given it differ in when the extrapolation is right and whether it can know it is, not in whether it ends right. Ren, 15 October 2026, did not take ‘situationally means the bound’ as theirs (“not sure what's the reading 1, but reality is always situational”); the reading's qualification is in identification-where-runs-part and typicality-by-counting.
